fatal_errors: The material is left as an unspecified HEA rather than identifying as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA with FCC and B2 phases.
The proposed high-pressure, high-temperature treatment is not the relevant intervention; the transition arises from intermediate-temperature aging at approximately 600°C and recovery near 750°C.
The hypothesis omits enhanced L12 ordering, jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries, planar slip, dislocation pile-ups, and phase-boundary-tip stress concentration.
No evidence supports pressure as a controlling variable.
The claimed general improvement in strength and ductility does not capture the observed ductility minimum at 600°C followed by recovery at 750°C.
explanation: The response recognizes that an HEA might display a ductile–brittle–ductile transition and supplies an appropriate conventional-alloy baseline, but it does not reconstruct the material, thermal-aging conditions, structural mediators, or mechanism. Its pressure-based treatment is an unsupported substitution. The proposed tensile and microstructural tests could establish whether a transition occurs, but they are not designed to distinguish the target mechanism through L12 ordering, jagged B2/FCC boundaries, dislocation pile-ups, or exclusion of impurity-segregation-driven intergranular fracture.
